notes: 8 pages matched /ai-|security-ai/. One page (security-ai, the category overview) maps onto the aisec source figure; the other seven need their own drawings because their stories are persona/verdict lanes (end-user GenAI, legal, EU AI Act, visibility assessment), agent-type funnels (agentic) or a Guard-in-the-path (homegrown) that no catalogue figure tells. The catalogue PNGs rendered with black filled boxes (CSS tokens missing in the headless render), so figure facts were checked against the FIGS source in kit-host.html rather than the pixels. aisec carries the engHead '← Single Pass Engine' back-button chip and a 'Full AI Security sheet ↗' gocomp chip, plus a KEY FEATURES chip 'Full sheet: AI Security' — all three are overview-app navigation and must be dropped for a static page. No journey (migration-journey-*) pages in this category.

steps.t: Employees reach public GenAI through the Cato Client or the browser plugin; usage is discovered first.
SPACE evaluates every prompt and upload against one AI policy set: audit, anonymise or block.
Homegrown apps and agents join the same engine through hooks, APIs and the AI Firewall.
Discovery, usage and violation reporting lands in the Cato Management Application.

security-ai.title: One AI Security engine for users, apps and agents
security-ai.desc: Five on-ramps — inline in the PoP, an existing proxy, API, LLM gateway and the browser plugin — feed one Cato AI Security engine whose detectors, profiles and actions govern employees' public AI tools, homegrown AI apps and AI agents alike, with every interaction logged as evidence.
security-ai.caption: One engine, three surfaces: employee prompts arrive inline or via the browser plugin, homegrown apps via API or an LLM gateway, agents via APIs and Scout. The same detectors and profile decide allow, anonymise, redirect, notify or block, and every interaction is logged for usage, risk and compliance reporting.
carry: Three surfaces named exactly as the page: AI for Users (browser plugin + Cato Client), AI for Applications (IDE integration + hooks), Agentic AI (APIs); the figure's three right-hand destinations must map one-to-one onto them
Policy evaluated by SPACE / the Single Pass Cloud Engine (current diagram node 'SPACE · CASB · DLP · TLS inspection')
Prompt-level auditing produces a prompt-level audit log; discovery is passive and does not read prompt content
Actions the page names: Monitor, Anonymize and Monitor, Block, Engage User, Redirect — the figure's Allow · Anonymise · Redirect · Notify user · Block pills are compatible
Figure fact 'Playground-tested' and 'prompts, responses and tool calls, in one pass' agree with the page; keep
Do NOT add the overview's '#1 in latency, accuracy and throughput' claim (only in the ai figure, not aisec) — the page does not make it
AI for End Users and AI for Applications are separate per-user licences (page prerequisite) — not drawn, but no label may imply one licence

steps.t: Deepfake fraud starts with a phishing message and ends with a stolen credential; both cross the PoP.
AI-orchestrated intrusions run the kill chain at machine speed; IPS virtual patching meets them in every PoP.
Shadow AI prompts and uploads are discovered, governed and anonymised rather than banned.
XDR correlates whatever survives each class into one incident story in the data lake.

diagram.brief: Three horizontal lanes, left-to-right: ATTACK CLASS → CATO SASE CLOUD (one shared popBox spanning all three lanes, centre, title 'Cato SASE Cloud', sub 'one pass · every flow · every user') → THE OUTCOME. Use tier() labels 'AI ATTACK CLASSES' (x 14) and 'THE OUTCOME' (x ~560) at the top. LEFT column, three nd boxes cls 'hot'/red-tinted via cloud(...,'bad') or nd with xmark: (1) 'Deepfake fraud' sub 'voice & video imposters'; (2) 'AI-orchestrated attacks' sub 'agents · AI malware'; (3) 'Shadow AI & data leak' sub 'prompts · rogue AI tools'. CENTRE inside the popBox, one engine chip row per lane aligned with its class: lane 1 chipRow 'SWG · DNS · NGAM · ZTNA' with f-s under it 'phishing & stolen creds'; lane 2 chipRow 'IPS virtual patching' + 'SPACE · XDR stories'; lane 3 chipRow 'AI Security suite' + 'Discovery · UIP · GenAI DLP' with f-s 'governed, not banned'. FLOWS: lanes 1 and 2 enter the PoP as fl-attack (red dashed) and terminate at an xmark() on the PoP boundary — these are blocked; lane 3 enters as fl-https (employee prompts) and continues THROUGH the PoP as fl-flow to its outcome with an amber pill 'anonymise · monitor' — this is governed, not blocked. RIGHT column, three nd boxes cls 'soft' with a mark(...,'ok'): (1) 'Fraud chain broken' sub 'callback checks stay human' (keep this honesty line verbatim: the fake face on the call is a people control, not a network one); (2) 'Machine speed matched' sub 'blast radius capped'; (3) 'Data stays home' sub 'AI adoption governed'. BOTTOM strip (y ~500): T f-s centred: 'Every class crosses the same single-pass engine — and XDR correlates whatever survives into one story', with a small nd 'XDR · data lake' (icon db) fed by three thin fl-net lines from the three lanes. ≤ 13 nodes. Keep lane colours: red for blocked attack classes, amber/limit for the governed lane, mint for outcomes. No incident names, no vendor logos; the nine incidents stay in the prose.

ai-threat-landscape.title: Three AI attack classes, one single-pass engine
ai-threat-landscape.desc: Deepfake fraud, AI-orchestrated attacks and shadow-AI data leakage each cross the same Cato PoP: the first two are broken at the network kill chain by SWG, DNS, anti-malware, ZTNA and IPS virtual patching, the third is discovered and governed rather than banned, and XDR correlates whatever survives into one story.

Outcome honesty lines: 'Fraud chain broken · callback checks stay human' (no network platform detects a fake face); 'Machine speed matched · blast radius capped'; 'Data stays home · AI adoption governed'

No incident names, dollar figures or CVE ids on the diagram (page prose carries EchoLeak CVE-2025-32711 etc.); diagram claims no detection of deepfake media

steps.t: Office and remote users' GenAI traffic already crosses the PoP; an optional browser extension adds depth.
TLS inspection, CASB/DLP and the AI Interaction Policy run in monitor mode: nothing is blocked.
Every sanctioned and shadow GenAI interaction is classified and logged across the four weeks.
The AI Security dashboards and GenAI Report become the board-ready AI risk report.

steps.t: AI Usage Discovery builds the inventory from Internet Firewall events the Cato Cloud already processes.
The User Interaction Policy inspects each prompt at the PoP: monitor, anonymise or block, per interaction.
The browser plugin enforces the same outcomes on managed devices Cato traffic never crosses.
Every decision is attributed and lands in the Overview and AI Users dashboards as evidence.

ai-genai-security.desc: Office, remote and off-net users reach sanctioned, embedded and shadow GenAI through the Cato PoP or the browser plugin, where the User Interaction Policy decides per prompt — allow and log, anonymise sensitive values, or block — and every decision lands in the dashboards as evidence.

steps.t: Scout scans developer endpoints for local coding agents, their configurations and MCP servers.
Managed agents on Bedrock, AI Foundry and Copilot Studio are discovered and traced via platform APIs.
Custom agents route their LLM calls via the AI Firewall proxy; Guards inspect prompts, outputs and tool calls.
Every session is recorded with violations tagged inline in Local Agents and Agent Sessions.

ai-agentic-security.title: Securing local, managed and custom AI agents
ai-agentic-security.desc: Local coding agents found by Scout, managed agents discovered through platform APIs and custom agents proxied through the AI Firewall all meet one control point, where Agent Policy and Guards inspect prompts, outputs, tool calls and tool messages, pass governed actions, block violations and record every session for audit.
carry: Three agent types with the page's examples: Local (coding agents on laptops; Scout + Agent Controls), Managed (AWS Bedrock · Azure AI Foundry · Microsoft Copilot Studio; platform APIs), Custom (LangChain · OpenAI Agents SDK · direct LLM API; AI-FW proxy endpoint via redirected LLM base URL + auth header)
Control point label: 'Cato AI Security · Agent Policy · AI-FW Guards'; four inspection points: prompts, outputs, tool calls, tool messages

Outcomes: 'Sanctioned systems · Repos · APIs · MCP tools' allowed; 'Risky action · Injected exfil attempt' blocked (indirect prompt injection through a tool response); 'Session telemetry · Agent Sessions · Audit · violations'
Discovery mechanisms are endpoint scanning (Scout, deployed via MDM: Intune, Jamf, Kandji; no TLS inspection, proxy or browser extension) and platform APIs — not network traffic
Two monitoring lenses: Local Agents (inventory & posture) and Agent Sessions (runtime behaviour)
Enforcement is documented at overview level only; the page's PoV runs monitor mode — the diagram may show a block (demo narrative) but the desc should not overclaim

steps.t: A homegrown chatbot, copilot or RAG app sends every prompt to a Cato Guard before it reaches a model.
The engine's detectors redact PII and forward benign prompts; injection and jailbreak attempts are blocked.
Cleared requests reach OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Bedrock or a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model.
Every session, verdict and analysis report is queryable in the Interaction Explorer; blocks alert the SOC.

Sanctioned assistants answer with client names masked; a restricted matter team's GenAI use is blocked.
Every redacted, monitored or blocked interaction is exportable as outside-counsel evidence.

steps.t: EU sites, the hybrid workforce and UK users whose AI output is used in the EU all cross a Cato PoP.
Shadow AI Discovery builds the deployer's AI inventory passively, without reading prompt content.
The User Interaction Policy allows, anonymises or blocks per prompt; org-classified prohibited use is blocked.
Events, Audit Trail and SIEM export are the supporting evidence; risk classification stays with governance.
